newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: Bolivia's oil firm to be split in 4 for sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia's oil firm to be split in 4 for sell-off.

text.p: Bolivia's oil company Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) will be split into four firms for its privatization tender, whose winners will be announced later Thursday, government sources said.
They added the government hopes to pocket a total of nearly $400 million from the sale of three of the four units.
Each of the four existing YPFB units will be turned into a new company.
The government will keep for itself the smallest one, a services and refining unit, which will still be called YPFB.
The three new exploration, production and transportation companies to be sold will be --
-- Chaco SAM, an exploration and production unit for which the government hopes to get at least its net worth value of $155 million.
-- Andina SAM, an exploration and production unit which should yield at least $130 million.
-- Empresa Transportadora de Hidrocarburos SAM, a transportation unit worth $98 million.

Under Boliviaos "capitalization" system, the winners will receive 50 percent of the shares and management control of each company. Rather than paying in cash for the stock they will have to invest the sum they bid to help capitalize the new firms.
Among those shortlisted to bid are Amoco, Mobil, Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Enron Corp, Argentina's energy firms YPF and Perez Companc, Canadaos Nova Gas and Spain's Repsol.
